description: The Building Performance Database is described by LBNL and DOE as the largest publicly available source of measured energy performance data for U.S. buildings, with records for over one million commercial and residential buildings. It combines, cleans and anonymises data from federal, state and local governments, utilities, efficiency programmes, building owners and companies; fields include location and climate zone, floor area, primary use, operating hours and occupants, lighting, heating and cooling system types, certifications such as ENERGY STAR and LEED, and energy use. Users build peer groups by type, location, size, age, equipment and operation, and compare them with statistical or actuarial methods through a web interface or an API. Coverage: the United States. Access: web application and API returning aggregate results. Licence: anonymised data shown only in aggregate; free. Caveats: the database is not a statistically representative sample like CBECS or RECS, and most records have only location, type and energy use. Simulation uses are peer benchmarks, energy use intensity distributions by type and climate, and targets for stock models. Related records: BEDES, the data dictionary the BPD uses, and SEED.
